title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the definitions begun on p.8 of an order-theoretic 'tronçon' (an ordered piece). It is the 1-dimensional building block for the combinatorial model of 'réseaux via découpages', meaning networks obtained by cutting.

Setting (p.8). L is an ordered set satisfying four axioms:
- (a) For a in L, any x, y > a admit z with x, y ≥ z > a. So the strict upper set of a is down-directed, with the witness staying strictly above a. Axiom (a') is the dual.
- (b) L is up- and down-directed.
- (c) Some axiom for x < y; as transcribed it is vacuous.
- (d) card L > 1.

Classification. L is a segment if it has both a least and a greatest element, and an interval if it has neither. This page completes the list: L is a half-interval ('demi-intervalle') if it has a least element but no greatest, or the reverse.

NB remarks:
- The opposite order of a tronçon, segment, interval or half-interval is again of the same kind.
- Opposition swaps 'closed on the left' with 'closed on the right'.
- Every tronçon is exactly one of segment, half-interval or interval. This is immediate, since the type is fixed by how many of min and max exist (2, 1 or 0); axiom (d) excludes min = max.

Boundary. ∂L is the set of elements that are the least or the greatest element. So |∂L| ∈ {0, 1, 2}, mirroring the topological boundary of [0,1], [0,1[ and ]0,1[.

Combinatorial data.
- S_0(L) = Drap_2(L) is the set of 2-element chains {x < y}.
- Modf(L) = Drap(L) is the set of all finite totally ordered subsets ('drapeaux', flags), i.e. the simplices of the order complex of L.

Purpose (next page). For a flag S = {s_1 < … < s_n}, the set C(S) of points comparable with all of S and not in S splits into 'connected components': L_{<s_1}, ]s_i, s_{i+1}[, L_{>s_n}, with boundaries {s_1}, {s_i, s_{i+1}}, {s_n}. In words, a finite set of cut points subdivides a 1-dimensional piece into sub-tronçons.

Grothendieck then claims that the 'bicoloured triangle' structure of a réseau (as in maps / dessins) can be recovered from structure (a) alone, plus (b) for T in S_0. This is part of his attempt at a purely combinatorial, order-theoretic foundation of tame ('modérée') topology for cut-up surfaces.
errors: Drap(L) is written as {S ⊂ P_f(L) | S totally ordered}; it should be S ∈ P_f(L) (or S ⊂ L finite).

The axioms do not force L to be totally ordered, which is why 'totalement ordonné' is needed in Drap. However, the description of connected components on the next page (open intervals between consecutive s_i) implicitly uses linear-order behaviour; the gap between the poset axioms and this linear picture is not addressed on this page.
Axiom (c) of p.8 as transcribed ('∃ z with x < z ≤ y') is trivially satisfied by z = y. Either the intended axiom differs (e.g. density or a local covering condition) or it is a slip.
Next page: 'Les seules non vides éventuellement étant L_{<s_1} … (si s_1 plus petit élément)' is garbled. If s_1 is the least element, L_{<s_1} is empty, not the only possibly non-empty piece.

ideas.what: Axiomatization of 1-dimensional ordered 'pieces' (tronçons) with local directedness axioms, and the trichotomy segment / half-interval / interval with boundary ∂L
ideas.modern_name: order-theoretic model of 1-cells / intervals of a linear continuum; generalized intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical order theory (Cantor, Dedekind for linear continua)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; related programmatic remarks on 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Flags Drap(L): finite chains of an ordered set, used as the combinatorial 'modifications' (cut-point configurations) of a tronçon
ideas.modern_name: order complex / nerve of a poset (chains as simplices)

ideas.what: Recovering the bicoloured-triangle (map / réseau) structure from order data on tronçons via cutting (découpages)
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial maps / dessins via flag structures; tame-topology foundations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses réseaux / cartographic groups, not this order-theoretic axiomatization

missed.claim: Grothendieck is building an order-theoretic (poset-based, possibly non-linear) axiomatics of 1-dimensional pieces, intended to rebuild 'réseaux' (bicoloured triangulations / maps) purely combinatorially. This is a concrete unpublished fragment of his tame-topology / dessins program; the direction was not systematically pursued in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: Toute tronçon est l'un des trois (segments, ½ intervalles, intervalles) à l'exclusion des deux autres.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with o-minimal and combinatorial approaches to tame topology and with flag-based descriptions of maps. The content of this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine definitions (the half-interval trichotomy, duality, boundary, chains / flags). Its interest lies solely in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished order-theoretic foundation for réseaux via découpages.
transcription_corrections: 'tranchée' should read 'tronçon' throughout, consistent with p.8 and the handwriting.
In 'Drap(L) = {S ⊂ P_f(L) …}' the image suggests S ∈ P_f(L) (or S ⊂ L finite); it is likely a notational slip in the original.
The diagonal margin note appears to involve '…tronçons binaires…'; it is largely illegible.
